notes: The one large source unit is אִישׁ רִיב → at ... strife. It is retained: one English word stands for the pair, the generic head noun owns no part of it, and rule 30's subtraction test is met, so fusing is preferable to leaving אִישׁ unrepresented beside a bare strife. Head on רִיב, the morpheme whose lexeme the word writes (rules 23, 30). The competing reading marks אִישׁ unrepresented.
The supplied at states what the bare predicate nominal contributes and joins that unit under rule 33; another preposition (in) would have served, so it is not the predicate's valency word.
וּ before בְנֵי עַמּוֹן takes the written with, which rule 14 lists among the connectives read off the ASV.

The waw of וָאֶזְעַק takes the pair and when as one rendering under rule 55, headed on the coordinator; the corpus heads eleven of twenty-seven such units on when instead, so that reading is available.
